item.title: NASSCO christens its final ‘floating pier’ ship in San Diego Bay
item.description: General Dynamics-NASSCO on Saturday christened the 784-foot USNS Hector A. Cafferata, Jr., the last of six super-sized sea-based platforms the company has built for the Navy.

item.title: Del Mar makes appointment to Design Review Board
item.description: The Del Mar City Council appointed Caitlin Laipenieks to the Design Review Board following a public interview during the March 5 council meeting. The board, which consists of five members, had one opening for a term running through March 31, 2030. Laipenieks, an attorney and Del Mar resident since 2020, was one of two applicants for a vacancy on the board, and the only one to interview during the council meeting. item.title: ‘Country’ Joe McDonald, ’60s rock star, proud protest counterculture icon, dies at 84
item.description: Joe McDonald, a hippie rock star of the 1960s “I-Feel-Like-I’m-Fixin’-To-Die Rag” was a four-lettered rebuke to the Vietnam War that became an anthem for protesters and a highlight of the Woodstock music festival, died Sunday. He was 84.

item.title: Santa Ana winds help set record highs in San Diego, Oceanside and Chula Vista
item.description: Hot, dry Santa Ana winds pushed the temperature to 89 degrees Sunday in San Diego, the highest temperature the city has recorded on March 8 since 1875 when the mercury hit 85, the National Weather Service said.
